item.title: Okinawa at New Year: Two New Years, Whale Season & a Day-by-Day Plan
item.description: Okinawa does New Year differently from the rest of Japan, in three ways that matter to a visitor. First, it is warm — daytime highs of 18–20°C, so this is the only part of Japan where you can spend January 1 outdoors in a light jacket. Second, there are two New Years: the solar one on January 1, observed nationally, and the lunar New Year (kyu-shogatsu) still celebrated in the fishing communities of Itoman, Motobu and the outer islands, where boats fly their full dress of fishing flags.
